en.title: Highest Substring Frequency Under Length and Character-Variety Limits
en.description:
Find the maximum number of times a substring occurs in the original string; occurrences may overlap. Candidate lengths are between minLength and maxLength, and the number of distinct characters must not exceed maxUnique; output 0 if there is no valid candidate.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains minLength maxLength maxUnique, and the second line contains the string. Original bounds: 2≤length≤100000, 2≤minLength≤maxLength≤26 and maxLength<string length, 2≤maxUnique≤26. The source does not restrict the character set; this site supports non-newline Unicode scalar characters, each character counts as one code point, and the total UTF-8 size is ≤400100 bytes.
en.explanation: The examples give 1, 3 and 3 respectively; ab occurs 3 times in ababab, and occurrences of aa may overlap.
hints: Count only windows of length minLength, filter out windows with too many distinct characters, and accumulate frequencies in a hash map.
